# bitcoin_io - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin-io/

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin I/O Library

The [ std::io](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html) module is not exposed in

`no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which
require reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this
library exists to export a minimal version of `std::io`’s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin`
so that we can support `no-std` applications.These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`’s traits without unnecessary complexity.

For examples of how to use and implement the types and traits in this crate see `io.rs` in the
`github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-bitcoin/bitcoin/examples/` directory.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub extern crate`- [hashes](https://docs.rs/bitcoin_hashes/0.20.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_hashes/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.Cursor.html)
- Wraps an in memory buffer providing `position`functionality for read and write.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The `io`crate error type.
- [FromStd](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the I/O traits for types that already implement `std`I/O traits.
- [Sink](https://docs.rs/struct.Sink.html)
- A sink to which all writes succeed.
- [Take](https://docs.rs/struct.Take.html)
- Reader adapter which limits the bytes read from an underlying reader.
- [ToStd](https://docs.rs/struct.ToStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the std traits for types that already implement our traits.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- A minimal subset of `std::io::ErrorKind``Error`
- [Read](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html)- Error
- An error that can occur when reading and decoding from a buffered reader.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [BufRead](https://docs.rs/trait.BufRead.html)
- A trait describing an input stream that uses an internal buffer when reading.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/trait.Read.html)
- A generic trait describing an input stream.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/trait.Write.html)
- A generic trait describing an output stream.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read.html)- from_ - read
- Decodes an object from a buffered reader.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a fixed-size buffer.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered_with.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered_ - with
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a custom-sized buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_to_writer.html)- to_ - writer
- Encodes a `consensus_encoding`object to an I/O writer.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std.html)- std
- Wraps a `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std_mut.html)- std_ - mut
- Wraps a mutable reference to `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_reader.html)- reader
- Hashes data from a reader.
- [sink](https://docs.rs/fn.sink.html)
- Returns a sink to which all writes succeed.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- Result type returned by functions in this crate.

# bitcoin_io - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin-io/0.5.0/bitcoin_io/

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin I/O Library

The [ std::io](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html) module is not exposed in

`no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which
require reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this
library exists to export a minimal version of `std::io`’s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin`
so that we can support `no-std` applications.These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`’s traits without unnecessary complexity.

For examples of how to use and implement the types and traits in this crate see `io.rs` in the

# bitcoin-io 0.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin-io/latest

# Rust-Bitcoin I/O Library

The `std::io` module is not exposed in `no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which require
reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this library exists
to export a minimal version of `std::io`'s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin` so that we can
support `no-std` applications.

These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`'s traits without unnecessary complexity.

# bitcoin_hashes - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin_hashes/^0.20.0/

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin Hashes Library

This library implements the hash functions needed by Bitcoin. As an ancillary thing, it exposes hexadecimal serialization and deserialization, since these are needed to display hashes.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Hashing a single byte slice or a string:

```
use bitcoin_hashes::Sha256;
let bytes = [0u8; 5];
let _hash_of_bytes = Sha256::hash(&bytes);
let _hash_of_string = Sha256::hash("some string".as_bytes());
```
Hashing content from a reader:

```
use bitcoin_hashes::Sha256;
let mut reader: &[u8] = b"hello"; // In real code, this could be a `File` or `TcpStream`.
let mut engine = Sha256::engine();
std::io::copy(&mut reader, &mut engine).expect("engine writes don't error");
let _hash = Sha256::from_engine(engine);
```
Hashing content using [ std::io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html) on a

`HashEngine`:```
use std::io::Write as _;
use bitcoin_hashes::Sha256;
let part1: &[u8] = b"hello";
let part2: &[u8] = b" ";
let part3: &[u8] = b"world";
let mut engine = Sha256::engine();
engine.write_all(part1).expect("engine writes don't error");
engine.write_all(part2).unwrap();
engine.write_all(part3).unwrap();
let _hash = Sha256::from_engine(engine);
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- A conversion trait for unsigned integer types smaller than or equal to 64-bits.

# bitcoin_io - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin-io/latest/target-redirect/bitcoin_io/

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin I/O Library

The [ std::io](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html) module is not exposed in

`no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which
require reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this
library exists to export a minimal version of `std::io`’s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin`
so that we can support `no-std` applications.These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`’s traits without unnecessary complexity.

For examples of how to use and implement the types and traits in this crate see `io.rs` in the
`github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-bitcoin/bitcoin/examples/` directory.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub extern crate`- [hashes](https://docs.rs/bitcoin_hashes/0.20.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_hashes/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.Cursor.html)
- Wraps an in memory buffer providing `position`functionality for read and write.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The `io`crate error type.
- [FromStd](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the I/O traits for types that already implement `std`I/O traits.
- [Sink](https://docs.rs/struct.Sink.html)
- A sink to which all writes succeed.
- [Take](https://docs.rs/struct.Take.html)
- Reader adapter which limits the bytes read from an underlying reader.
- [ToStd](https://docs.rs/struct.ToStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the std traits for types that already implement our traits.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- A minimal subset of `std::io::ErrorKind``Error`
- [Read](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html)- Error
- An error that can occur when reading and decoding from a buffered reader.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [BufRead](https://docs.rs/trait.BufRead.html)
- A trait describing an input stream that uses an internal buffer when reading.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/trait.Read.html)
- A generic trait describing an input stream.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/trait.Write.html)
- A generic trait describing an output stream.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- Decodes an object from a buffered reader.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a fixed-size buffer.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered_with.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered_ - with
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a custom-sized buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_to_writer.html)- to_ - writer
- Encodes a `consensus_encoding`object to an I/O writer.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std.html)- std
- Wraps a `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std_mut.html)- std_ - mut
- Wraps a mutable reference to `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_reader.html)- reader
- Hashes data from a reader.
- [sink](https://docs.rs/fn.sink.html)
- Returns a sink to which all writes succeed.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# bitcoin_hashes - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin_hashes/0.20.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_hashes/index.html

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin Hashes Library

This library implements the hash functions needed by Bitcoin. As an ancillary thing, it exposes hexadecimal serialization and deserialization, since these are needed to display hashes.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Hashing a single byte slice or a string:

```
use bitcoin_hashes::Sha256;
let bytes = [0u8; 5];
let _hash_of_bytes = Sha256::hash(&bytes);
let _hash_of_string = Sha256::hash("some string".as_bytes());
```
Hashing content from a reader:

```
use bitcoin_hashes::Sha256;
let mut reader: &[u8] = b"hello"; // In real code, this could be a `File` or `TcpStream`.
let mut engine = Sha256::engine();
std::io::copy(&mut reader, &mut engine).expect("engine writes don't error");
let _hash = Sha256::from_engine(engine);
```
Hashing content using [ std::io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html) on a

`HashEngine`:```
use std::io::Write as _;
use bitcoin_hashes::Sha256;
let part1: &[u8] = b"hello";
let part2: &[u8] = b" ";
let part3: &[u8] = b"world";
let mut engine = Sha256::engine();
engine.write_all(part1).expect("engine writes don't error");
engine.write_all(part2).unwrap();
engine.write_all(part3).unwrap();
let _hash = Sha256::from_engine(engine);
```

# synth-verify - Formal Verification for Synth Compiler

Formal verification infrastructure for the Synth WebAssembly-to-ARM compiler using SMT-based translation validation.

## Overview

This crate provides:

- **SMT-based translation validation**using Z3 SMT solver
- **Formal semantics**for WebAssembly and ARM operations
- **Property-based testing**framework with proptest
- **Automated verification**of synthesis rules

## Architecture

```
synth-verify/
├── wasm_semantics.rs      # WASM → SMT encoding (25+ operations)
├── arm_semantics.rs       # ARM → SMT encoding (processor state model)
├── translation_validator.rs # Equivalence prover (Alive2-inspired)
└── properties.rs          # Property-based tests (50+ properties)
```
## Usage

### Verifying a Synthesis Rule

```
use ;
use ;
// Create Z3 context
let ctx = create_z3_context;
let validator = new;
// Define a synthesis rule
let rule = SynthesisRule ;
// Verify the rule
match validator.verify_rule
```
### Batch Verification

```
// Verify multiple rules
let rules = vec!;
let results = validator.verify_rules;
for  in results
```
### Property-Based Testing

```
use CompilerProperties;
use *;
proptest!
```
## Verification Approach

### Translation Validation

For each synthesis rule `WASM_OP → ARM_OPS`, we prove:

```
∀inputs. ⟦WASM_OP⟧(inputs) = ⟦ARM_OPS⟧(inputs)
```
Using SMT solver:

- Create symbolic inputs
- Encode WASM semantics: `φ_wasm`
- Encode ARM semantics: `φ_arm`
- Assert: `φ_wasm ≠ φ_arm`
- Check satisfiability:
- **UNSAT**→ Proven correct
- **SAT**→ Counterexample found
- **UNKNOWN**→ Timeout

### Example: ADD Verification

```
; Symbolic inputs
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 32))
; WASM: i32.add
(define-fun wasm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; ARM: ADD R0, R0, R1
(define-fun arm-add () (_ BitVec 32)
  (bvadd a b))
; Prove equivalence
(assert (not (= wasm-add arm-add)))
(check-sat)  ; Returns: unsat → Proven!
```
## Verified Operations

| Operation | Status | Method |
|---|---|---|
| i32.add | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.sub | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.mul | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_s | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.div_u | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.and | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.or | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.xor | ✓ Proven | SMT |
| i32.shl | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_u | ⚠ Partial | Complex |
| i32.shr_s | ⚠ Partial | Complex |

## Dependencies

### Required

- **z3**- Z3 SMT solver Rust bindings (v0.12)
- **synth-synthesis**- Synthesis rules and operations
- **proptest**- Property-based testing

### System Requirements

Z3 requires either:

- System installation: `libz3-dev`or`z3`package
- Static linking: Built automatically (requires C++ compiler)

For development without Z3:

```
# Skip tests that require Z3
```
## Testing

```
# Run all tests (requires Z3)
# Run specific test suites
# Property-based testing with more cases
PROPTEST_CASES=10000
```
## Performance

- Verification time: 50-500ms per rule (SMT solving)
- Memory usage: ~50MB (Z3 context)
- Scalability: Linear in number of rules

## Limitations

- **Shift operations**: Modulo handling complex for SMT
- **Control flow**: Branch verification requires extended modeling
- **Memory operations**: Requires memory model formalization
- **Floating point**: Not yet supported

## Future Work

### Phase 1: Complete SMT Coverage

- Shift operation verification
- Control flow (branches, conditions)
- Memory operations (load/store)

### Phase 2: Optimization Verification

- DCE, constant folding, CSE correctness
- Loop optimization soundness
- Register allocation preservation

### Phase 3: Mechanized Proofs

- Port to Coq proof assistant
- Machine-checked correctness
- Certified synthesis rule library

## References

- **Alive2**: Automated LLVM verification (Lopes et al., PLDI 2021)
- **CompCert**: Verified C compiler (Leroy, POPL 2006)
- **VeriISLE**: Verified instruction selection (Nandi et al., PLDI 2020)
- **Z3**: Efficient SMT solver (de Moura & Bjørner, TACAS 2008)

PulseEngine Team

# thingd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thingd/0.47.0/thingd/

## Expand description

Core primitives for thingd.

This crate owns the durable engine boundary: object storage, append-only
events, and queue storage. The default implementation is in-memory, with a
feature-gated `SQLite` adapter available for durable object, event, and
queue storage.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sqlite` | No | Enables with FTS5 search, WAL mode, and auto-migration`SqliteThingStore` |
| `connectors` | No | Enables CSV/JSON file connectors for data import |

[§](https://docs.rs#example-in-memory)Example (in-memory)

```
use thingd::{MemoryEngine, ObjectStore, EventLog, MemoryObject, MemoryEvent};
let mut engine = MemoryEngine::new();
let obj = MemoryObject::new("users", "alice", r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
engine.put_object(obj).unwrap();
let user = engine.get_object("users", "alice").unwrap();
assert_eq!(user.unwrap().body, r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
let event = MemoryEvent::new("audit", "user.created", r#"{"user":"alice"}"#);
engine.append_event(event).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-sqlite--requires-sqlite-feature)Example (`SQLite` — requires `sqlite` feature)

```
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
{
    use thingd::{SqliteThingStore, ObjectStore, MemoryObject};
    let mut db = SqliteThingStore::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    db.put_object(MemoryObject::new("users", "alice", r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#)).unwrap();
    let user = db.get_object("users", "alice").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(user.unwrap().body, r#"{"name":"Alice"}"#);
}
```

# synth_backend_riscv - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synth-backend-riscv/0.25.0/synth_backend_riscv/

## Expand description

RISC-V backend for synth — RV32IMAC encoder, ELF builder, PMP allocator.

Mirrors the structure of `synth-backend` (ARM Cortex-M) but emits RISC-V
machine code. The instruction selector lives in `synth-synthesis::riscv`;
this crate contains the binary encoder, ELF emission, linker script
generation, and Physical Memory Protection (PMP) allocator.

Supported variants (per `TargetSpec::IsaVariant::RiscV32 { extensions }`):

- RV32I — base 32-bit integer
- RV32IM — adds multiply/divide
- RV32IMA — adds atomics
- RV32IMAC — adds compressed (16-bit) instructions

The encoder always emits 32-bit instructions in this skeleton. The 16-bit C-extension encoding will be a peephole pass in a follow-up.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use backend::`- [RiscVBackend](https://docs.rs/backend/struct.RiscVBackend.html);

- [Provisioner](https://docs.rs/enum.ProvisionerOutgoingMessages.html)- Outgoing - Messages
- [PvfChecker](https://docs.rs/enum.PvfCheckerOutgoingMessages.html)- Outgoing - Messages

- An error that may happen during Availability Recovery process.
- [Runtime](https://docs.rs/enum.RuntimeApiError.html)- ApiError
- A description of an error causing the runtime API request to be unservable.
- [Runtime](https://docs.rs/enum.RuntimeApiOutgoingMessages.html)- ApiOutgoing - Messages
- [Statement](https://docs.rs/enum.StatementDistributionOutgoingMessages.html)- Distribution - Outgoing - Messages
- [Subsystem](https://docs.rs/enum.SubsystemError.html)- Error
- An error type that describes faults that may happen
- [ToOrchestra](https://docs.rs/enum.ToOrchestra.html)
- A type of messages that are sent from a `Subsystem`
- [TrySend](https://docs.rs/enum.TrySendError.html)- Error
- A bounded channel error when trying to send a message (transparently wraps the inner error type)

# synth_backend_aarch64 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synth-backend-aarch64/0.25.0/synth_backend_aarch64/

## Expand description

AArch64 (A64) host-native backend for synth — **milestone 1** (#538).

Goal (from #538): a minimal A64 integer-subset backend reachable via
`-b aarch64`, so synth output runs and debugs natively on arm64 dev hosts
(Apple Silicon, arm64 Linux/CI) instead of only under QEMU/Renode — and so a
third backend becomes a third differential oracle against the Thumb-2 and RV32
lowerings.

[§](https://docs.rs#milestone-status)Milestone status

- **1a (this crate, now):**the verified A64- *encoder*(integer data-processing +- `movz`/- `movk`+- `ret`, cross-checked against- `clang`) and a minimal straight-line- *selector*(params in- `w0..w7`, i32 add/sub/mul/and/or/xor + const, result to- `w0`,- `ret`).- `compile_bytes`turns a leaf integer function’s wasm ops into A64 machine code. Ops outside the subset return- `Unsupported`— an honest loud-skip, never wrong code.
- **1b (next):**an- `EM_AARCH64`relocatable-ELF emitter, the- `Backend`trait impl,- `-b aarch64`CLI wiring, and the native differential-execution acceptance probe (- `synth compile add.wat -b aarch64`→ link + run on the arm64 host, diff vs wasmtime).
- **later:**spilling, i64, floats, memory, control flow, calls, DWARF.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use backend::`- [AArch64Backend](https://docs.rs/backend/struct.AArch64Backend.html);
- `pub use selector::`- [SelectError](https://docs.rs/selector/struct.SelectError.html);
- `pub use selector::`- [select](https://docs.rs/selector/fn.select.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)
- `Backend`trait implementation for the AArch64 host-native backend (#538).
- [elf](https://docs.rs/elf/index.html)
- Minimal `EM_AARCH64`ELF64 relocatable-object emitter — milestone-1b (#538).
- [encoder](https://docs.rs/encoder/index.html)
- Minimal AArch64 (A64) instruction encoder — milestone-1 integer subset (#538).
- [selector](https://docs.rs/selector/index.html)
- Minimal AArch64 instruction selector — milestone-1 integer subset (#538).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compile_](https://docs.rs/fn.compile_bytes.html)- bytes
- Lower a single leaf integer function (wasm ops + declared param count) to A64
machine-code bytes (little-endian 32-bit words). Convenience over
`selector::select``.text`bytes.

# synth_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/synth-backend/0.25.0/synth_backend/

## Expand description

Synth Backend - Code generation and binary emission

Generic scaffolding (ELF builder, linker scripts, memory layout) is always
available. ARM-specific modules are behind the `arm-cortex-m` feature.

- [Wasm](https://docs.rs/struct.WasmGlobal.html)- Global
- A WASM global’s declaration — its initial value and mutability (#237).
Needed so the native-pointer ABI can recognize a global whose initializer is
a linear-memory address (e.g. `$__stack_pointer = 65536`) and make it`__synth_wasm_data`-relative, rather than reading it from an R9 globals table the self-contained drop-in object can’t rely on.

- WASM linear memory specification

# odcs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/odcs/0.9.0/odcs/

## Expand description

Reference implementation of the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS).

[ SPEC.md](https://docs.rs/SPEC.md) at the repository root defines the upstream specification
policy. This crate implements the foundational pipeline:

`ODCS Document → Parser → Canonical Object Model → Validator → Diagnostics`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use odcs::{parse, validate, DocumentFormat};
let yaml = br#"
version: "1.0.0"
apiVersion: "v3.1.0"
kind: "DataContract"
id: "example"
status: "draft"
"#;
let result = parse(yaml, DocumentFormat::Yaml);
let contract = result.contract.expect("parse succeeded");
let report = validate(&contract);
assert!(report.is_valid());
```

# bitcoin-io 0.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin-io/0.5.0

# Rust-Bitcoin I/O Library

The `std::io` module is not exposed in `no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which require
reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this library exists
to export a minimal version of `std::io`'s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin` so that we can
support `no-std` applications.

These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`'s traits without unnecessary complexity.

---

                Simple I/O traits for no-std (and std) environments

# bitcoin_io - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin-io/0.5.0/target-redirect/bitcoin_io/

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin I/O Library

The [ std::io](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html) module is not exposed in

`no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which
require reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this
library exists to export a minimal version of `std::io`’s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin`
so that we can support `no-std` applications.These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`’s traits without unnecessary complexity.

For examples of how to use and implement the types and traits in this crate see `io.rs` in the
`github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-bitcoin/bitcoin/examples/` directory.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub extern crate`- [hashes](https://docs.rs/bitcoin_hashes/0.20.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_hashes/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.Cursor.html)
- Wraps an in memory buffer providing `position`functionality for read and write.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The `io`crate error type.
- [FromStd](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the I/O traits for types that already implement `std`I/O traits.
- [Sink](https://docs.rs/struct.Sink.html)
- A sink to which all writes succeed.
- [Take](https://docs.rs/struct.Take.html)
- Reader adapter which limits the bytes read from an underlying reader.
- [ToStd](https://docs.rs/struct.ToStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the std traits for types that already implement our traits.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- A minimal subset of `std::io::ErrorKind``Error`
- [Read](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html)- Error
- An error that can occur when reading and decoding from a buffered reader.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [BufRead](https://docs.rs/trait.BufRead.html)
- A trait describing an input stream that uses an internal buffer when reading.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/trait.Read.html)
- A generic trait describing an input stream.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/trait.Write.html)
- A generic trait describing an output stream.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read.html)- from_ - read
- Decodes an object from a buffered reader.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a fixed-size buffer.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered_with.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered_ - with
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a custom-sized buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_to_writer.html)- to_ - writer
- Encodes a `consensus_encoding`object to an I/O writer.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std.html)- std
- Wraps a `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std_mut.html)- std_ - mut
- Wraps a mutable reference to `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_reader.html)- reader
- Hashes data from a reader.
- [sink](https://docs.rs/fn.sink.html)
- Returns a sink to which all writes succeed.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- Result type returned by functions in this crate.

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin I/O Library

The [ std::io](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html) module is not exposed in

require reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this
library exists to export a minimal version of `std::io`’s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin`
so that we can support `no-std` applications.These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`’s traits without unnecessary complexity.

For examples of how to use and implement the types and traits in this crate see `io.rs` in the
`github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-bitcoin/bitcoin/examples/` directory.

[73](#73)    fn read_exact(&mut self, mut buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<()> {
[74](#74)        while !buf.is_empty() {
[75](#75)            match self.read(buf) {
[76](#76)                Ok(0) => return Err(ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof.into()),
[77](#77)                Ok(len) => buf = &mut buf[len..],
[78](#78)                Err(e) if e.kind() == ErrorKind::Interrupted => {}
[79](#79)                Err(e) => return Err(e),
[80](#80)            }
[81](#81)        }
[82](#82)        Ok(())
[83](#83)    }
[84](#84)
[85](#85)    #[inline]
[87](#87)    fn take(self, limit: u64) -> Take<Self>
[88](#88)    where
[89](#89)        Self: Sized,
[90](#90)    {
[91](#91)        Take { reader: self, remaining: limit }
[92](#92)    }
[93](#93)
[94](#94)    #[doc(alias = "read_to_end")]
[109](#109)    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[110](#110)    #[inline]
[111](#111)    fn read_to_limit(&mut self, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, limit: u64) -> Result<usize> {
[112](#112)        self.take(limit).read_to_end(buf)
[113](#113)    }
[114](#114)}
[115](#115)
[116](#116)pub trait BufRead: Read {
[118](#118)    fn fill_buf(&mut self) -> Result<&[u8]>;
[124](#124)
[125](#125)    fn consume(&mut self, amount: usize);
[131](#131)}
[132](#132)
[133](#133)#[derive(Debug)]
[137](#137)pub struct Take<R> {
[138](#138)    reader: R,
[139](#139)    remaining: u64,
[140](#140)}
[141](#141)
[142](#142)impl<R: Read> Take<R> {
[143](#143)    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[155](#155)    #[inline]
[156](#156)    pub fn read_to_end(&mut self, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<usize> {
[157](#157)        let mut read: usize = 0;
[158](#158)        let mut chunk = [0u8; 64];
[159](#159)        loop {
[160](#160)            match self.read(&mut chunk) {
[161](#161)                Ok(0) => break,
[162](#162)                Ok(n) => {
[163](#163)                    buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[0..n]);
[164](#164)                    read += n;
[165](#165)                }
[166](#166)                Err(ref e) if e.kind() == ErrorKind::Interrupted => {}
[167](#167)                Err(e) => return Err(e),
[168](#168)            };
[169](#169)        }
[170](#170)        Ok(read)
[171](#171)    }
[172](#172)}
[173](#173)
[174](#174)impl<R: Read> Read for Take<R> {
[175](#175)    #[inline]
[176](#176)    fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize> {
[177](#177)        let len = cmp::min(buf.len(), self.remaining.try_into().unwrap_or(buf.len()));
[178](#178)        let read = self.reader.read(&mut buf[..len])?;
[179](#179)        self.remaining -= read.try_into().unwrap_or(self.remaining);
[180](#180)        Ok(read)
[181](#181)    }
[182](#182)}
[183](#183)
[184](#184)impl<R: BufRead> BufRead for Take<R> {
[186](#186)    #[inline]
[187](#187)    fn fill_buf(&mut self) -> Result<&[u8]> {
[188](#188)        if self.remaining == 0 {
[190](#190)            return Ok(&[]);
[191](#191)        }
[192](#192)
[193](#193)        let buf = self.reader.fill_buf()?;
[194](#194)        let cap = cmp::min(buf.len() as u64, self.remaining) as usize;
[197](#197)        Ok(&buf[..cap])
[198](#198)    }
[199](#199)
[200](#200)    #[inline]
[201](#201)    fn consume(&mut self, amount: usize) {
[202](#202)        assert!(amount as u64 <= self.remaining);
[203](#203)        self.remaining -= amount as u64;
[204](#204)        self.reader.consume(amount);
[205](#205)    }
[206](#206)}
[207](#207)

[211](#211)

[224](#224)impl Read for &[u8] {
[225](#225)    #[inline]
[226](#226)    fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize> {
[227](#227)        let cnt = cmp::min(self.len(), buf.len());
[228](#228)        buf[..cnt].copy_from_slice(&self[..cnt]);
[229](#229)        *self = &self[cnt..];
[230](#230)        Ok(cnt)

[293](#293)
[294](#294)impl<T: AsRef<[u8]>> Read for Cursor<T> {
[295](#295)    #[inline]
[296](#296)    fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize> {
[297](#297)        let inner: &[u8] = self.inner.as_ref();
[298](#298)        let start_pos = self.pos.try_into().unwrap_or(inner.len());
[299](#299)        if start_pos >= self.inner.as_ref().len() {
[300](#300)            return Ok(0);
[301](#301)        }
[302](#302)
[303](#303)        let read = core::cmp::min(inner.len().saturating_sub(start_pos), buf.len());
[304](#304)        buf[..read].copy_from_slice(&inner[start_pos..start_pos + read]);
[305](#305)        self.pos = self.pos.saturating_add(read.try_into().unwrap_or(u64::MAX ));
[306](#306)        Ok(read)
[307](#307)    }
[308](#308)}
[309](#309)
[310](#310)impl<T: AsRef<[u8]>> BufRead for Cursor<T> {
[311](#311)    #[inline]
[312](#312)    fn fill_buf(&mut self) -> Result<&[u8]> {
[313](#313)        let inner: &[u8] = self.inner.as_ref();
[314](#314)        let pos = self.pos.min(inner.len() as u64) as usize;
[315](#315)        Ok(&inner[pos..])
[316](#316)    }
[317](#317)
[318](#318)    #[inline]
[319](#319)    fn consume(&mut self, amount: usize) { self.pos = self.pos.saturating_add(amount as u64); }
[320](#320)}
[321](#321)
[322](#322)impl<T: AsMut<[u8]>> Write for Cursor<T> {
[323](#323)    #[inline]
[324](#324)    fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {
[325](#325)        let write_slice = self.inner.as_mut();
[326](#326)        let pos = cmp::min(self.pos, write_slice.len() as u64);
[327](#327)        let amt = (&mut write_slice[(pos as usize)..]).write(buf)?;
[328](#328)        self.pos += amt as u64;
[329](#329)        Ok(amt)
[330](#330)    }
[331](#331)
[332](#332)    #[inline]
[333](#333)    fn flush(&mut self) -> Result<()> { Ok(()) }

[367](#367)                Err(e) => return Err(e),
[368](#368)            }
[369](#369)        }
[370](#370)        Ok(())
[371](#371)    }

[447](#447)pub fn encode_to_writer<T, W>(object: &T, mut writer: W) -> Result<()>
[453](#453)where
[454](#454)    T: encoding::Encodable + ?Sized,
[455](#455)    W: Write,
[456](#456){
[457](#457)    let mut encoder = object.encoder();
[458](#458)    loop {
[459](#459)        writer.write_all(encoder.current_chunk())?;
[460](#460)        if !encoder.advance() {

[466](#466)
[467](#467)pub fn decode_from_read<T, R>(
[480](#480)    mut reader: R,
[481](#481)) -> core::result::Result<T, ReadError<<T::Decoder as Decoder>::Error>>
[482](#482)where
[483](#483)    T: Decodable,
[484](#484)    R: BufRead,
[485](#485){
[486](#486)    let mut decoder = T::decoder();
[487](#487)
[488](#488)    loop {
[489](#489)        let mut buffer = match reader.fill_buf() {
[490](#490)            Ok(buffer) => buffer,
[491](#491)            Err(error) if error.kind() == ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
[493](#493)            Err(error) => return Err(ReadError::Io(error)),
[494](#494)        };
[495](#495)
[496](#496)        if buffer.is_empty() {
[497](#497)            return decoder.end().map_err(ReadError::Decode);
[499](#499)        }
[500](#500)
[501](#501)        let original_len = buffer.len();
[502](#502)        let need_more = decoder.push_bytes(&mut buffer).map_err(ReadError::Decode)?;
[503](#503)        let consumed = original_len - buffer.len();
[504](#504)        reader.consume(consumed);
[505](#505)
[506](#506)        if !need_more {
[507](#507)            return decoder.end().map_err(ReadError::Decode);
[508](#508)        }
[509](#509)    }
[510](#510)}
[511](#511)
[512](#512)pub fn decode_from_read_unbuffered<T, R>(
[531](#531)    reader: R,
[532](#532)) -> core::result::Result<T, ReadError<<T::Decoder as Decoder>::Error>>
[533](#533)where
[534](#534)    T: Decodable,
[535](#535)    R: Read,
[536](#536){
[537](#537)    decode_from_read_unbuffered_with::<T, R, 4096>(reader)
[538](#538)}
[539](#539)
[540](#540)pub fn decode_from_read_unbuffered_with<T, R, const BUFFER_SIZE: usize>(
[558](#558)    mut reader: R,
[559](#559)) -> core::result::Result<T, ReadError<<T::Decoder as Decoder>::Error>>
[560](#560)where
[561](#561)    T: Decodable,
[562](#562)    R: Read,
[563](#563){
[564](#564)    let mut decoder = T::decoder();
[565](#565)    let mut buffer = [0u8; BUFFER_SIZE];
[566](#566)
[567](#567)    while decoder.read_limit() > 0 {
[568](#568)        let clamped_buffer = &mut buffer[..decoder.read_limit().min(BUFFER_SIZE)];
[570](#570)        match reader.read(clamped_buffer) {
[571](#571)            Ok(0) => {
[572](#572)                return decoder.end().map_err(ReadError::Decode);
[574](#574)            }
[575](#575)            Ok(bytes_read) => {
[576](#576)                if !decoder
[577](#577)                    .push_bytes(&mut &clamped_buffer[..bytes_read])
[578](#578)                    .map_err(ReadError::Decode)?
[579](#579)                {
[580](#580)                    return decoder.end().map_err(ReadError::Decode);
[581](#581)                }
[582](#582)            }
[583](#583)            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == ErrorKind::Interrupted => {
[584](#584)                }
[586](#586)            Err(e) => return Err(ReadError::Io(e)),
[587](#587)        }
[588](#588)    }
[589](#589)
[590](#590)    decoder.end().map_err(ReadError::Decode)
[591](#591)}
[592](#592)

# Cursor in bitcoin_io - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin-io/0.5.0/bitcoin_io/struct.Cursor.html

`pub struct Cursor<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Wraps an in memory buffer providing `position` functionality for read and write.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bitcoin_io/lib.rs.html#266)#### pub fn [set_position](https://docs.rs#method.set_position)(&mut self, position: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bitcoin_io/lib.rs.html#266)

#### pub fn [set_position](https://docs.rs#method.set_position)(&mut self, position: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

Sets the internal position.

This method allows seeking within the wrapped memory by setting the position.

Note that setting a position that is larger than the buffer length will cause reads to succeed by reading zero bytes. Further, writes will be no-op zero length writes.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bitcoin_io/lib.rs.html#272)#### pub fn [into_inner](https://docs.rs#method.into_inner)(self) -> T

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/bitcoin_io/lib.rs.html#272)

#### pub fn [into_inner](https://docs.rs#method.into_inner)(self) -> T

Returns the inner buffer.

This is the whole wrapped buffer, including the bytes already read.

Returns a reference to the inner buffer.

This is the whole wrapped buffer, including the bytes already read.

# ErrorKind in bitcoin_io - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin-io/0.5.0/bitcoin_io/enum.ErrorKind.html

```
pub enum ErrorKind {
```
## Show 18 variants

    NotFound,
    PermissionDenied,
    ConnectionRefused,
    ConnectionReset,
    ConnectionAborted,
    NotConnected,
    AddrInUse,
    AddrNotAvailable,
    BrokenPipe,
    AlreadyExists,
    WouldBlock,
    InvalidInput,
    InvalidData,
    TimedOut,
    WriteZero,
    Interrupted,
    UnexpectedEof,
    Other,
}## Expand description

A minimal subset of [ std::io::ErrorKind](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/enum.ErrorKind.html) which is used for

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)

`Error`Note that, as with [ std::io](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html), only

[has defined semantics in this crate, all other variants are provided here only to provide higher-fidelity conversions to and from](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.Interrupted)

`Self::Interrupted`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)

`std::io::Error`## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NotFound)

### NotFound

An entity was not found, often a file.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.PermissionDenied)

### PermissionDenied

The operation lacked the necessary privileges to complete.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ConnectionRefused)

### ConnectionRefused

The connection was refused by the remote server.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ConnectionReset)

### ConnectionReset

The connection was reset by the remote server.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ConnectionAborted)

### ConnectionAborted

The connection was aborted (terminated) by the remote server.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NotConnected)

### NotConnected

The network operation failed because it was not connected yet.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AddrInUse)

### AddrInUse

A socket address could not be bound because the address is already in use elsewhere.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AddrNotAvailable)

### AddrNotAvailable

A nonexistent interface was requested or the requested address was not local.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BrokenPipe)

### BrokenPipe

The operation failed because a pipe was closed.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AlreadyExists)

### AlreadyExists

An entity already exists, often a file.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.WouldBlock)

### WouldBlock

The operation needs to block to complete, but the blocking operation was requested to not occur.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidInput)

### InvalidInput

A parameter was incorrect.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidData)

### InvalidData

Data not valid for the operation were encountered.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TimedOut)

### TimedOut

The I/O operation’s timeout expired, causing it to be canceled.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.WriteZero)

### WriteZero

An error returned when an operation could not be completed because a call to `write` returned `Ok(0)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Interrupted)

### Interrupted

This operation was interrupted.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnexpectedEof)

### UnexpectedEof

An error returned when an operation could not be completed because an “end of file” was reached prematurely.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Other)

### Other

A custom error that does not fall under any other I/O error kind

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

}## Expand description

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Constructs a new adapter which will read at most `limit` bytes.

Attempts to read up to limit bytes from the reader, allocating space in `buf` as needed.

`limit` is used to prevent a denial of service attack vector since an unbounded reader will
exhaust all memory.

Similar to [ std::io::Read::read_to_end](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html#method.read_to_end) but with the DOS protection.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns-1)Returns

The number of bytes read if successful or an [ Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html) if reading fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

If an I/O error occurs while reading from the underlying reader.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

Decodes an object from a buffered reader.

# decode_from_read_unbuffered in bitcoin_io - Rust

```
pub fn decode_from_read_unbuffered<T, R>(
    reader: R,
) ->
```
[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [ReadError](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html)<<T::[Decoder](https://docs.rs/bitcoin-consensus-encoding/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_consensus_encoding/decode/trait.Decodable.html#associatedtype.Decoder) as [Decoder](https://docs.rs/bitcoin-consensus-encoding/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_consensus_encoding/decode/trait.Decoder.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/bitcoin-consensus-encoding/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_consensus_encoding/decode/trait.Decoder.html#associatedtype.Error)>>## Expand description

Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a fixed-size buffer.

For most use cases, prefer [ decode_from_read](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read.html) with a

[. This function is only needed when you have an unbuffered reader which you cannot wrap. It will probably have worse performance.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/buffered/bufreader/struct.BufReader.html)

`std::io::BufReader`[§](https://docs.rs#buffer)Buffer

Uses a fixed 4KB (4096 bytes) stack-allocated buffer that is reused across read operations. This size is a good balance between memory usage and system call efficiency for most use cases.

For different buffer sizes, use [ decode_from_read_unbuffered_with](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered_with.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ ReadError::Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Decode) if the decoder encounters an error while parsing
the data, or

[if an I/O error occurs while reading.](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Io)

`ReadError::Io`

`pub fn decode_from_read_unbuffered_with<T, R, const BUFFER_SIZE: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(

Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a custom-sized buffer.

For most use cases, prefer [ decode_from_read](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read.html) with a

[. This function is only needed when you have an unbuffered reader which you cannot wrap. It will probably have worse performance.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/buffered/bufreader/struct.BufReader.html)

`std::io::BufReader`[§](https://docs.rs#buffer)Buffer

The `BUFFER_SIZE` parameter controls the intermediate buffer size used for
reading. The buffer is allocated on the stack (not heap) and reused across
read operations. Larger buffers reduce the number of system calls, but use
more memory.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ ReadError::Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Decode) if the decoder encounters an error while parsing
the data, or

[if an I/O error occurs while reading.](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Io)

`ReadError::Io`

# bitcoin_io - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin-io/latest/bitcoin_io/

## Expand description

Rust Bitcoin I/O Library

The [ std::io](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html) module is not exposed in

`no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which
require reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this
library exists to export a minimal version of `std::io`’s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin`
so that we can support `no-std` applications.These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`’s traits without unnecessary complexity.

For examples of how to use and implement the types and traits in this crate see `io.rs` in the
`github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-bitcoin/bitcoin/examples/` directory.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub extern crate`- [hashes](https://docs.rs/bitcoin_hashes/0.20.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bitcoin_hashes/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.Cursor.html)
- Wraps an in memory buffer providing `position`functionality for read and write.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The `io`crate error type.
- [FromStd](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the I/O traits for types that already implement `std`I/O traits.
- [Sink](https://docs.rs/struct.Sink.html)
- A sink to which all writes succeed.
- [Take](https://docs.rs/struct.Take.html)
- Reader adapter which limits the bytes read from an underlying reader.
- [ToStd](https://docs.rs/struct.ToStd.html)
- A bridging wrapper providing the std traits for types that already implement our traits.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- A minimal subset of `std::io::ErrorKind``Error`
- [Read](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html)- Error
- An error that can occur when reading and decoding from a buffered reader.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [BufRead](https://docs.rs/trait.BufRead.html)
- A trait describing an input stream that uses an internal buffer when reading.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/trait.Read.html)
- A generic trait describing an input stream.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/trait.Write.html)
- A generic trait describing an output stream.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read.html)- from_ - read
- Decodes an object from a buffered reader.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a fixed-size buffer.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered_with.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered_ - with
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a custom-sized buffer.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_to_writer.html)- to_ - writer
- Encodes a `consensus_encoding`object to an I/O writer.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std.html)- std
- Wraps a `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_std_mut.html)- std_ - mut
- Wraps a mutable reference to `std`I/O type to implement the traits from this crate.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_reader.html)- reader
- Hashes data from a reader.
- [sink](https://docs.rs/fn.sink.html)
- Returns a sink to which all writes succeed.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

# bitcoin-io 0.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin-io/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# Bitcoin Consensus Encoding

This crate provides traits that can be used to encode/decode objects in a consensus-consistent way.

`consensus_encoding 0.1.0`

This is the start of the `v1.0.0` release candidate cycle. We will
endeavour to not release breaking changes unless totally necessary and
will honour semver rules as usual. From this release forward we will
semver trick as possible in subsequent releases to assist downstream
users testing these releases.

Thanks for your patience and help.

# bitcoin_hashes 0.20.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin_hashes/^0.20.0

# Bitcoin Hashes Library

This is a simple, no-dependency library which implements the hash functions needed by Bitcoin. These are SHA1, SHA256, SHA256d, SHA512, and RIPEMD160. As an ancillary thing, it exposes hexadecimal serialization and deserialization, since these are needed to display hashes anyway.

## Contributions

Contributions are welcome, including additional hash function implementations.

### Githooks

To assist devs in catching errors *before* running CI we provide some githooks. If you do not
already have locally configured githooks you can use the ones in this repository by running, in the
root directory of the repository:

```
```
Alternatively add symlinks in your `.git/hooks` directory to any of the githooks we provide.

### Running Benchmarks

We use a custom Rust compiler configuration conditional to guard the benchmark code. To run the
benchmarks use: `RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=bench' cargo +nightly bench`.

# Rust-Bitcoin IO Library

The `std::io` module is not exposed in `no-std` Rust so building `no-std` applications which require
reading and writing objects via standard traits is not generally possible. Thus, this library exists
to export a minmal version of `std::io`'s traits which we use in `rust-bitcoin` so that we can
support `no-std` applications.

These traits are not one-for-one drop-ins, but are as close as possible while still implementing
`std::io`'s traits without unnecessary complexity.

---

```
It was found that the `1.0.0-rc.x` releases were troublesome because
of how `cargo` resolves version numbers that include a suffix. For
this reason we elected to go back to pre-1.0 version numbers.
`v0.5.0` is a re-release of `v0.4.0-rc.0`. The only change is to
update the other `rust-bitcoin` repo dependencies.
*
* ********
* ***
*
* *
Create the `io` crate, add basic I/O traits, types, and implementations.
Traits:

Types:

Empty crate to reserve the name on crates.io

# Bitcoin Consensus Encoding

This crate provides traits that can be used to encode/decode objects in a consensus-consistent way.

`consensus_encoding 0.1.0`

This is the start of the `v1.0.0` release candidate cycle. We will
endeavour to not release breaking changes unless totally necessary and
will honour semver rules as usual. From this release forward we will
semver trick as possible in subsequent releases to assist downstream
users testing these releases.

Thanks for your patience and help.

# hex_conservative - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hex-conservative/^0.3.0/

## Expand description

Hex encoding and decoding.

General purpose hex encoding/decoding library with a conservative MSRV and dependency policy.

[§](https://docs.rs#const-hex-literals)Const hex literals

```
use hex_conservative::hex;
const GENESIS: [u8; 32] = hex!("000000000019d6689c085ae165831e934ff763ae46a2a6c172b3f1b60a8ce26f");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-hex-parsing)Runtime hex parsing

```
// In your manifest use the `package` key to improve import ergonomics.
// hex = { package = "hex-conservative", version = "*" }
use hex::prelude::*;
// Decode an arbitrary length hex string into a vector.
let v = Vec::from_hex("deadbeef").expect("valid hex digits");
// Or a known length hex string into a fixed size array.
let a = <[u8; 4]>::from_hex("deadbeef").expect("valid length and valid hex digits");
// We support `LowerHex` and `UpperHex` out of the box for `[u8]` slices.
println!("An array as lower hex: {:x}", a.as_hex());
// And for vecs since `Vec` derefs to byte slice.
println!("A vector as upper hex: {:X}", v.as_hex());
// Allocate a new string (also `to_upper_hex_string`).
let s = v.to_lower_hex_string();
// Please note, mixed case strings will still parse successfully but we only
// support displaying hex in a single case.
assert_eq!(
    Vec::from_hex("dEaDbEeF").expect("valid mixed case hex digits"),
    Vec::from_hex("deadbeef").expect("valid hex digits"),
);
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [buf_](https://docs.rs/buf_encoder/index.html)- encoder
- Implements a buffered encoder.
- [display](https://docs.rs/display/index.html)
- Helpers for displaying bytes as hex strings.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error code for the `hex-conservative`crate.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)
- Hex encoding and decoding.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Re-exports of the common crate traits.
- [serde](https://docs.rs/serde/index.html)- `serde`
- Hex encoding with `serde`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [fmt_](https://docs.rs/macro.fmt_hex_exact.html)- hex_ - exact
- Format known-length array as hex.
- [hex](https://docs.rs/macro.hex.html)
- Parses hex strings in const contexts.
- [impl_](https://docs.rs/macro.impl_fmt_traits.html)- fmt_ - traits
- Adds `core::fmt`trait implementations to type`$ty`.
- [test_](https://docs.rs/macro.test_hex_unwrap.html)- hex_ - unwrap
- Quick and dirty macro for parsing hex in tests.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/macro.write_err.html)- err
- Formats error.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.BytesToHexIter.html)- ToHex - Iter
- Iterator over bytes which encodes the bytes and yields hex characters.
- [HexTo](https://docs.rs/struct.HexToBytesIter.html)- Bytes - Iter
- Iterator yielding bytes decoded from an iterator of pairs of hex digits.
- [Invalid](https://docs.rs/struct.InvalidCharError.html)- Char - Error
- Invalid hex character.
- [OddLength](https://docs.rs/struct.OddLengthStringError.html)- String - Error
- Purported hex string had odd length.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Case](https://docs.rs/enum.Case.html)
- Possible case of hex.
- [HexTo](https://docs.rs/enum.HexToArrayError.html)- Array - Error
- Hex decoding error.
- [HexTo](https://docs.rs/enum.HexToBytesError.html)- Bytes - Error
- Hex decoding error.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Display](https://docs.rs/trait.DisplayHex.html)- Hex
- Extension trait for types that can be displayed as hex.
- [FromHex](https://docs.rs/trait.FromHex.html)
- Trait for objects that can be deserialized from hex strings.

- Convenience alias for `HexToBytesIter<HexDigitsIter<'a>>`.

# bitcoin_consensus_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin-consensus-encoding/latest/target-redirect/bitcoin_consensus_encoding/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rust-bitcoin-consensus-encoding)Rust Bitcoin Consensus Encoding

Traits and utilities for encoding and decoding Bitcoin data types in a consensus-consistent way,
using a *sans-I/O* architecture.

Rather than reading from or writing to [ std::io::Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)/

[traits directly, the codec types work with byte slices. This keeps codec logic I/O-agnostic, so the same implementation works in](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)

`std::io::Write``no_std` environments, sync I/O, async I/O, and hash engines without
duplicating logic or surfacing I/O errors in non-I/O contexts (e.g. when hashing an encoding).*Consensus* encoding is the canonical byte representation of Bitcoin data types used across the
peer-to-peer network and transaction serialization. This crate only supports deterministic
encoding and will never support types like floats whose encoding is non-deterministic or
platform-dependent.

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding)Encoding

Types implement [ Encode](https://docs.rs/trait.Encode.html) to produce an

[, which yields encoded bytes in chunks via](https://docs.rs/trait.Encoder.html)

`Encoder`[and](https://docs.rs/trait.Encoder.html#tymethod.current_chunk)

`Encoder::current_chunk`[. The caller drives the process by pulling chunks until](https://docs.rs/trait.Encoder.html#tymethod.advance)

`Encoder::advance``advance` returns [.](https://docs.rs/enum.EncoderStatus.html#variant.Finished)

`EncoderStatus::Finished`[§](https://docs.rs#decoding)Decoding

Types implement [ Decode](https://docs.rs/trait.Decode.html) to produce a

[, which consumes bytes via](https://docs.rs/trait.Decoder.html)

`Decoder`[until it signals completion by returning](https://docs.rs/trait.Decoder.html#tymethod.push_bytes)

`Decoder::push_bytes``Ok(DecoderStatus::Ready)`. The
caller then calls [to obtain the decoded value.](https://docs.rs/trait.Decoder.html#tymethod.end)

`Decoder::end`Unlike encoding, decoding is fallible. Both `push_bytes` and `end` return `Result`. I/O errors
are handled by the caller, keeping the codec logic I/O-agnostic.

[§](https://docs.rs#drivers)Drivers

This crate provides free functions which drive codecs for common I/O interfaces. On the decoding side we provide:

- `decode_from_read`
- `decode_from_read_unbuffered`
- `decode_from_read_unbuffered_with`
- `decode_from_slice`
- `decode_from_slice_unbounded`

And on the encoding side we provide:

- `encode_to_writer`
- `drain_to_writer`
- `encode_to_vec`
- `drain_to_vec`

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `std`- Enables std lib I/O driver functions and- `std::error::Error`impls (implies- `alloc`).
- `alloc`- Enables- `encode_to_vec`- `Vec`-based decoders, and allocation-based helpers.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayDecoder.html)- Decoder
- A decoder that expects exactly N bytes and returns them as an array.
- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayEncoder.html)- Encoder
- An encoder for a single array.
- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayRefEncoder.html)- RefEncoder
- An encoder for a reference to an array.
- [Byte](https://docs.rs/struct.ByteVecDecoder.html)- VecDecoder
- A decoder that decodes a byte vector.
- [Bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.BytesEncoder.html)- Encoder
- An encoder for a single byte slice.
- [Compact](https://docs.rs/struct.CompactSizeDecoder.html)- Size - Decoder
- Decodes a compact size encoded integer as a length prefix.
- [Compact](https://docs.rs/struct.CompactSizeEncoder.html)- Size - Encoder
- Encoder for a compact size encoded integer.
- [Compact](https://docs.rs/struct.CompactSizeU64Decoder.html)- Size - U64Decoder
- Decodes a compact size encoded integer as a raw `u64`.
- [Decoder2](https://docs.rs/struct.Decoder2.html)
- A decoder which wraps two inner decoders and returns the output of both.
- [Decoder3](https://docs.rs/struct.Decoder3.html)
- A decoder which decodes three objects, one after the other.
- [Decoder4](https://docs.rs/struct.Decoder4.html)
- A decoder which decodes four objects, one after the other.
- [Decoder6](https://docs.rs/struct.Decoder6.html)
- A decoder which decodes six objects, one after the other.
- [Encoder2](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoder2.html)
- An encoder which encodes two objects, one after the other.
- [Encoder3](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoder3.html)
- An encoder which encodes three objects, one after the other.
- [Encoder4](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoder4.html)
- An encoder which encodes four objects, one after the other.
- [Encoder6](https://docs.rs/struct.Encoder6.html)
- An encoder which encodes six objects, one after the other.
- [Encoder](https://docs.rs/struct.EncoderByteIter.html)- Byte - Iter
- Yields bytes from any `Encoder`
- [Slice](https://docs.rs/struct.SliceEncoder.html)- Encoder
- An encoder for a list of encodable types.
- [VecDecoder](https://docs.rs/struct.VecDecoder.html)
- A decoder that decodes a vector of `T`s.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Decoder](https://docs.rs/enum.DecoderStatus.html)- Status
- Indicates whether a decoder needs more data or is ready to finalize.
- [Encoder](https://docs.rs/enum.EncoderStatus.html)- Status
- Indicates whether the encoder still has bytes available or it is finished.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Decode](https://docs.rs/trait.Decode.html)
- A Bitcoin object which can be consensus-decoded using a push decoder.
- [Decoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Decoder.html)
- A push decoder for a consensus-decodable object.
- [Encode](https://docs.rs/trait.Encode.html)
- A Bitcoin object which can be consensus-encoded.
- [Encoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Encoder.html)
- An encoder for a consensus-encodable object.
- [Exact](https://docs.rs/trait.ExactSizeEncoder.html)- Size - Encoder
- An encoder with a known size.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_decode.html)- decode
- Checks that the given bytes decode to the expected value, panicking if they don’t.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_decoder.html)- decoder
- Checks that the given `decoder`produces the expected value, panicking if it doesn’t.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_encode.html)- encode
- Checks that the given `value`encodes to`expected`, panicking if it doesn’t.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_encoder.html)- encoder
- Checks that the given `encoder`yields`expected`, panicking if it doesn’t.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read.html)- from_ - read
- Decodes an object from a buffered reader.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a fixed-size buffer.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered_with.html)- from_ - read_ - unbuffered_ - with
- Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a custom-sized buffer.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_slice.html)- from_ - slice
- Decodes an object from a byte slice.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_slice_unbounded.html)- from_ - slice_ - unbounded
- Decodes an object from an unbounded byte slice.
- [drain_](https://docs.rs/fn.drain_to_vec.html)- to_ - vec
- Drains the output of an `Encoder`
- [drain_](https://docs.rs/fn.drain_to_writer.html)- to_ - writer
- Drains the output of an `Encoder`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_to_vec.html)- to_ - vec
- Encodes an object into a vector.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_to_writer.html)- to_ - writer
- Encodes an object to a standard I/O writer.

# ExactSizeEncoder in bitcoin_consensus_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin-consensus-encoding/^0.1.0/trait.ExactSizeEncoder.html

`pub trait ExactSizeEncoder: `[Encoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Encoder.html) {
    // Required method

    Second(B),
    Third(C),
    Fourth(D),
    Fifth(E),
    Sixth(F),
}
```

# decode_from_read in bitcoin_consensus_encoding - Rust

## Expand description

Decodes an object from a buffered reader.

[§](https://docs.rs#performance)Performance

For unbuffered readers (like [ std::fs::File](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.File.html) or

[), consider wrapping your reader with](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/net/tcp/struct.TcpStream.html)

`std::net::TcpStream`[in order to use this function. This avoids frequent small reads, which can significantly impact performance.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/buffered/bufreader/struct.BufReader.html)

`std::io::BufReader`[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ ReadError::Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Decode) if the decoder encounters an error while parsing
the data, or

[if an I/O error occurs while reading.](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Io)

`ReadError::Io`

# decode_from_read_unbuffered_with in bitcoin_consensus_encoding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bitcoin-consensus-encoding/^0.1.0/fn.decode_from_read_unbuffered_with.html

`pub fn decode_from_read_unbuffered_with<T, R, const BUFFER_SIZE: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(
    reader: R,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [ReadError](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html)<<T::[Decoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Decodable.html#associatedtype.Decoder) as [Decoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Decoder.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/trait.Decoder.html#associatedtype.Error)>>## Expand description

Decodes an object from an unbuffered reader using a custom-sized buffer.

For most use cases, prefer [ decode_from_read](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_from_read.html) with a

[. This function is only needed when you have an unbuffered reader which you cannot wrap. It will probably have worse performance.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/buffered/bufreader/struct.BufReader.html)

`std::io::BufReader`[§](https://docs.rs#buffer)Buffer

The `BUFFER_SIZE` parameter controls the intermediate buffer size used for
reading. The buffer is allocated on the stack (not heap) and reused across
read operations. Larger buffers reduce the number of system calls, but use
more memory.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ ReadError::Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Decode) if the decoder encounters an error while parsing
the data, or

[if an I/O error occurs while reading.](https://docs.rs/enum.ReadError.html#variant.Io)

`ReadError::Io`

# bitcoin_hashes 0.20.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitcoin_hashes/0.20.0

# Bitcoin Hashes Library

This is a simple, no-dependency library which implements the hash functions needed by Bitcoin. These are SHA1, SHA256, SHA256d, SHA512, and RIPEMD160. As an ancillary thing, it exposes hexadecimal serialization and deserialization, since these are needed to display hashes anyway.

## Contributions

Contributions are welcome, including additional hash function implementations.

### Githooks

To assist devs in catching errors *before* running CI we provide some githooks. If you do not
already have locally configured githooks you can use the ones in this repository by running, in the
root directory of the repository:

```
```
Alternatively add symlinks in your `.git/hooks` directory to any of the githooks we provide.

### Running Benchmarks

We use a custom Rust compiler configuration conditional to guard the benchmark code. To run the
benchmarks use: `RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=bench' cargo +nightly bench`.
